question: Intranasal corticosteroids (INCS) are the most effective single pharmacological therapy for persistent allergic rhinitis in children and should be the cornerstone of pharmacological management when symptoms are moderate-severe.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. A common misconception is that oral antihistamines are the primary treatment because they relieve sneezing and itch rapidly. However, antihistamines have little effect on nasal congestion and do not address late-phase inflammation. INCS address all four cardinal nasal symptoms and are ARIA-recommended first-line pharmacotherapy for moderate-severe persistent allergic rhinitis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. INCS (e.g. fluticasone propionate, mometasone furoate) act locally to suppress the full inflammatory cascade in the nasal mucosa — both the early-phase histamine-mediated response and the late-phase cellular inflammation. Multiple RCTs and ARIA guidelines confirm INCS superiority over oral antihistamines for all nasal symptoms, particularly congestion. They are safe when used at recommended doses with correct technique.
